class_name: 推量-高確実性-ノダロウ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1: author → mechanical attachment gate → cold review → fixes applied → gate re-run

patterns.usage_note: のだ + だろう, contracted to んだろう in speech: unlike bare だろう it conjectures about the explanation behind something the speaker has just observed, so it typically follows a stated or implied piece of evidence. Polite んでしょう and written のだろう are the same pattern. It attaches to plain forms, and with na-adjectives and nouns the copula must surface as な (静かなんだろう), not だ.

examples.ruby: 電気[でんき]が消[き]えているから、もう寝[ね]たんだろう。
examples.english: The lights are off, so he must have gone to bed already.

examples.ruby: 返事[へんじ]がないから、たぶん忙[いそが]しいんだろう。
examples.english: There's been no reply, so she's probably busy.

examples.ruby: あの顔[かお]を見[み]る限[かぎ]り、もう本当[ほんとう]のことを知[し]っているんでしょう。
examples.english: Judging by that face, I take it he already knows the truth.

patterns.usage_note: A written-style, emotionally colored conjecture: it adds the speaker's sympathy, admiration or wistfulness to what plain だろう would state flatly, so it very often pairs with さぞ(かし) or どんなに. Use it when you are imagining someone else's feelings or a scene you cannot see; for a neutral prediction about facts, use だろう. The contracted こったろう survives mainly in the fixed exclamation なんてこったろう; ことでしょう is the polite counterpart.

examples.ruby: 一人[ひとり]で異国[いこく]の地[ち]に立[た]った時[とき]、心細[こころぼそ]かったことだろう。
examples.english: Standing alone in a foreign land, how forlorn she must have felt.

examples.ruby: 合格[ごうかく]の知[し]らせに、どんなに喜[よろこ]んだことだろう。
examples.english: How overjoyed she must have been at the news that she'd passed.

examples.ruby: 桜[さくら]が咲[さ]けば、さぞ美[うつく]しいことでしょう。
examples.english: Once the cherry trees bloom, it will surely be a lovely sight.

patterns.usage_note: The everyday conjecture marker, historically a contraction of である + う. It states the speaker's own estimate of a fact, with none of the explanatory framing of んだろう or the emotional coloring of ことだろう. Attached directly to nouns and na-adjective stems with no copula (明日は雨だろう), and said with rising intonation it becomes a confirmation-seeking tag; でしょう is the polite form, だろ／でしょ the casual clipped ones.

examples.ruby: この店[みせ]のラーメンは子[こ]どもには少[すこ]し辛[から]いだろう。
examples.english: The ramen at this place will probably be a little too spicy for the kids.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は今[いま]ごろプールで泳[およ]いでいるだろう。
examples.english: My little sister is off swimming at the pool about now, I expect.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の朝[あさ]は山[やま]の上[うえ]が白[しろ]くなっているでしょう。
examples.english: By tomorrow morning the mountaintop will most likely be white.

patterns.usage_note: The bare conjectural う, attached to the 未然ウ接続 stem. In contemporary Japanese it survives as a live conjecture mainly in であろう (from ある) and in i-adjective forms such as よかろう・なかろう・高かろう; on ordinary verbs the same ending is read as volitional (行こう) instead. It belongs to formal writing and deliberately old-fashioned speech, where だろう would be the neutral choice; よかろう in particular has drifted beyond prediction into a curt granting of permission or recommendation ('that'll do', 'do as you like'); other adjective forms such as 高かろう・なかろう stay purely conjectural.

examples.ruby: その話[はなし]はおそらく事実[じじつ]であろう。
examples.english: That account is in all likelihood true.

examples.ruby: 今[いま]は何[なに]も言[い]わずに待[ま]つのがよかろう。
examples.english: It would be best to say nothing for now and wait.

examples.ruby: この案[あん]なら誰[だれ]にも異論[いろん]はなかろう。
examples.english: No one is likely to object to this proposal.

patterns.usage_note: Auxiliary 得る on the masu-stem marks logical possibility rather than acquired ability: it is the written equivalent of 〜可能性がある／〜ということもある, not of できる, so 泳ぎ得る cannot mean 'I can swim'. Dictionary and prenominal forms are read either うる or える (起こり得る), but every other form uses え-: the negative is only 得ない (えない), never うない. あり得る／あり得ない are the highest-frequency instances.

examples.ruby: この方法[ほうほう]でも問題[もんだい]は解決[かいけつ]し得[う]る。
examples.english: This approach, too, could conceivably solve the problem.

examples.ruby: 薬[くすり]の飲[の]み合[あ]わせによっては、強[つよ]い副作用[ふくさよう]もあり得[え]ます。
examples.english: Depending on how the medicines combine, serious side effects are entirely possible.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]にでも起[お]こり得[う]る単純[たんじゅん]な失敗[しっぱい]だ。
examples.english: It's a simple slip that could happen to anyone.
